chapter: Radio, Jazz Record and Blue Note (Reel 2)
title: The WNYC radio show and the complaint that he was commercial
summary: Hodes describes his WNYC radio program, where a station manager complained he was commercial. He kept the show anyway, and says listeners still remember it.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Get that bum off the air, he's commercial. Now, I'm not getting a penny salary. I'm either buying my own records or they're being furnished to me. I'm paying my own carfare, I'm paying my own lunch. All they're doing is giving me an announcer and a turntable guy, that's there anyway. And this man is accusing me of being commercial.

So there was no talking to the guy. The guy that was running the station, there was no way in the world you could talk to that little fire rat. So they just warned me, cool it, on the announcing. There was no way I could cool it. I didn't have no secretary, I was getting letters. I had an audience of a million kids or so, from around New York, New England.

What amazes me is, so many of those kids that were listening then still remember. I've seen it happen over and over again, in concerts and like this engagements. People come up and say, I used to listen to that.
I listened to that program. Pee Wee Russell --
It's converted a lot of people.
